title: Sources, repository pins and the novelty gate
question: Which occult, Schumann and contact links have actually been documented or measured?
result: Selected current public repository files and primary studies were inspected. Official Bashar material does name frequency bands; the earlier blanket no-Hz attribution was corrected. No admitted synchronized Schumann/contact dataset or authenticated ET source was found in the inspected material.
critique: Recent text-similarity, EEG-spectrum and SR/physiology papers already cover nearby ideas. Proceed as evidence and methods engineering; the next test must specify a physical input and receiver.

title: Dimensioned electromagnetic acquisition
question: What can the stated magnetic signal induce in a specified ideal coil?
result: The illustrative 1 pT RMS, 7.83 Hz field gives 49.1973 nV RMS for 1,000 turns of 1 m². Producer 65 assertions and 151 independent comparisons passed, including zero-sensitivity cases.
critique: A stipulated coil and resistor-only noise model are not a feasible detector, tissue dose, biological response or sender identifier. Next, test timing and lag-selection artifacts.

title: Lag selection exposes a powerless toy
question: Does correcting for searched lags control a known finite randomization null?
result: One 32-offset fixture gave 7/32 rejections for the invalid selected-lag test. The adjusted test gave none. Independent review proved its minimum possible adjusted p was 7/32, so it could never reject at 0.05. The distinct-shape null fixture and all-lag p = 1 control were retained.
critique: Correct calibration alone is not useful sensitivity. Preserve the failure and predeclare a larger group; real calendar dependence still needs its own justified null.

benchmark.label: Round 3 / preserved limitation
benchmark.title: A correct test can be unable to detect anything.
benchmark.result: Seven searched lags across 32 cyclic offsets force corrected p ≥ 7/32. At α = 0.05 this design cannot reject for any input. The invalid selected-lag test nevertheless rejected 7/32 offsets in one fixture.
benchmark.limit: Zero adjusted rejections are not evidence that an effect is absent. This is a synthetic finite-group demonstration, not an empirical anomaly detector.

title: Resolve test granularity; expose a common cause
question: Can a larger finite test detect alignment, and does alignment identify a mechanism?
result: The separately versioned 256-offset design permits an aligned p = 7/256. Both producer fixtures retain 7/256 adjusted null rejections, with naive counts 77/256 and 75/256. In the shared-driver example, observational rank is 1 with nullity 1; only a stipulated independent perturbation gives rank 2.
critique: The sensitivity example is not a population-power estimate. More sensors or calendar labels do not establish the independent-intervention premise. Next, separate information accuracy from agency.

benchmark.label: Round 4 / two distinct limits
benchmark.title: Better statistical resolution does not identify the cause.
benchmark.result: With 256 offsets, the aligned example reaches p = 7/256 = 0.02734375. Yet X = z, Y = 2z fits both Y = 2X and a shared-driver model. Their observational design has kernel (1, −1). A hypothetical independent perturbation produces rank 2 and Gram determinant 28.
benchmark.limit: The cyclic null and hypothetical intervention are assumptions. These calculations do not validate them for actual field recordings or channeling reports.

title: Hidden information, leakage and numerical repair
question: What would a fixed concealed-target score establish, and how does leakage change it?
result: For 100 actual four-choice guesses under the declared null, the 5% rejection threshold is 33 hits. An ordinary independent leak with probability 0.2 gives the same q = 0.4 hit-count law as any stipulated independent mechanism with q = 0.4. A positive-tail underflow defect was reproduced, archived and repaired before acceptance.
critique: At 40 hits and 10 compromised trials, the preselected-subset tail is 0.0472839, while the arbitrary-after-outcome corruption bound is 0.149541. Actual leakage is unknown. Next, require custody, chronology and data provenance without pretending metadata authenticates them.

benchmark.label: Round 5 / fixed-trial arithmetic
benchmark.title: A score cannot name its information source.
benchmark.result: For 40/100 four-choice guesses, the specified no-information tail is 0.000686592. With m = 10 assumed compromised trials, the preselected-subset model gives 0.0472839 and the arbitrary-outcome-corruption bound gives 0.149541. A 20% perfect-leak mixture has q = 0.4 and the same count distribution as another independent source with q = 0.4.
benchmark.limit: There were no human trials. The actual leakage count is unknown. Exact binomial scoring assumes a guess on every trial; pre-reveal abstentions retained as nonhits require the conservative-reference distinction in the protocol. No ET probability follows.

title: Adversarial evidence intake and a prospective protocol
question: Can a complete-looking packet incorrectly become authenticated contact evidence?
result: The staged validator separates documentary, environmental, information and paired metadata readiness. A fully fabricated packet can satisfy structural requirements but always remains unauthenticated. Actual quick-look/Kp/corpus availability descriptors do not become paired evidence. One published target digest was matched by hashing four candidate strings.
critique: Hashes identify checked bytes, not truthful timestamps or secrecy. Declared nonce length does not prove entropy. A ready packet still requires independent calibration and custody review. Stop after these six rounds; acquire discriminating evidence before another discovery cycle.

benchmark.label: Round 6 / metadata is not authentication
benchmark.title: Keep an attractive packet from certifying itself.
benchmark.result: Malformed units, dates, Nyquist settings, reveal chronology, trial counts and unpaired intervals are challenged independently. Complete fabricated observational metadata can be structurally ready while evidenceAuthenticated remains false. The four-target unsalted-hash demonstration recovers the selected target by enumeration.
benchmark.limit: This is not a cryptographic break or proof that a salted scheme is secure. The code does not fetch or authenticate referenced data, calibrations, randomness, custody or subjective reports.
